scope: A coarse milestone abstraction for one recorded attachment episode and its follow-up snapshot. Ever reached and final present are different facts. Sources span trace/snapshot reporting, not a common physical wire clock. Entry means admission to USB4-domain operation, including compatible mode where applicable; it does not mean a native Enter_USB packet was captured. Failure-stage rows partition the modeled unfinished milestone, not the root cause. Exit is a cross-cutting event. Logical combinations have no assigned probability.

fact_provenance.E: C11/C12: cached device status cannot separate skipped entry from exit; no fresh entry witness.
fact_provenance.L: C04/C19: no qualified usable-link history; no-router checks are not never-link evidence.
fact_provenance.R: C04: final absence and sampled No checks do not prove an operational router never existed transiently.
fact_provenance.F: ASUS-COMPARE /asus_external_routers =0 in the recorded normal failed comparison snapshot.
fact_provenance.X: C11/C12: NotAttemptedOrExited is not an ordered exit witness.
fact_provenance.C: Pinned ASUS-COMMANDS/ASUS-COMPLETIONS/ASUS-ERRORS establish10 commands,10 terminal completions and zero CCI error/busy/unsupported. A failed quality rule would leave C unknown.

ideal_observations.caveat: A qualified positive link-ready sample can witness this. A negative current sample cannot prove never-ready; that requires validated event/history coverage.
Requires an understood entry/history witness. A cached NotAttemptedOrExited code is unknown; an inferred domain milestone is not a captured native Enter_USB request/Accept.
Requires a fresh, correctly owned operational-router witness. A cached node, a capability bit or merely identifying a register is insufficient.
Requires understood ordered history. Exit may occur before usable link/router creation; later re-entry is allowed. No captured exit is unknown without complete coverage.
